claim: 17-Hydroxygeranylinalool diterpene glycosides (DTGs) are abundant herbivory-induced, structurally diverse and commonly malonylated defense metabolites in Nicotiana attenuata plants.
source: 17-Hydroxygeranylinalool diterpene glycosides (DTGs) are abundant herbivory-induced, structurally diverse and commonly malonylated defense metabolites in Nicotiana attenuata plants.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by references to previous work throughout the manuscript.

claim: Silencing NaMaT1 results in DTG-dependent reduced floral style lengths.
source: By identifying and silencing a malonyltransferase, NaMaT1, involved in DTG malonylation, we found that DTG malonylation percentages are normally remarkably uniform, but when disrupted, result in DTG-dependent reduced floral style lengths
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Reduced style lengths in NaMaT1-silenced plants result from reduced stylar cell sizes.
source: which in turn result from reduced stylar cell sizes, IAA contents, and YUC activity
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by microscopy data in Figure 3B-D.

claim: Reduced style lengths in NaMaT1-silenced plants result from reduced IAA contents.
source: which in turn result from reduced stylar cell sizes, IAA contents, and YUC activity
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by phytohormone measurements shown in Figure 4D and Figure 5.

claim: Reduced style lengths in NaMaT1-silenced plants result from reduced YUC activity.
source: which in turn result from reduced stylar cell sizes, IAA contents, and YUC activity
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by enzyme activity assays shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The short-style phenotype of NaMaT1-silenced plants can be restored by IAA supplementation.
source: phenotypes that could be restored by IAA supplementation or by silencing the DTG pathway
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally in Figure 5D.

claim: The short-style phenotype of NaMaT1-silenced plants can be restored by silencing the DTG pathway.
source: phenotypes that could be restored by IAA supplementation or by silencing the DTG pathway
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by VIGS experiments in irGGPPS background shown in Figure 3.

claim: The Nicotiana genus-specific JA-deficient short-style phenotype results from alterations in DTG malonylation patterns.
source: Moreover, the Nicotiana genus-specific JA-deficient short-style phenotype also results from alterations in DTG malonylation patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments with irAOC plants shown in Figure 6.

claim: DTG malonylation percentages are remarkably uniform across development, treatments, and tissue types.
source: In this study, we discovered that the malonylation percentage of DTGs is remarkably uniform across development, treatments, and tissue types
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Malonylation of anthocyanins enhances pigment stability and color intensity at the pH of the intracellular milieus.
source: Malonylation of anthocyanins enhances pigment stability and color intensity at the pH of the intracellular milieus (Suzuki et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Suzuki et al., 2002.

claim: Malonylated anthocyanins are preferentially transported to vacuoles in Arabidopsis thaliana.
source: In addition, malonylated anthocyanins are preferentially transported to vacuoles in Arabidopsis thaliana (Zhao et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhao et al., 2011.

claim: The malonylation of glycosides is catalyzed by malonyltransferases, members of the biochemically versatile BAHD acyltransferase family.
source: The malonylation of glycosides is catalyzed by malonyltransferases, members of the biochemically versatile BAHD acyltransferase family (D'Auria, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to D'Auria, 2006.

claim: The in vivo functions of malonyltransferases are largely unknown.
source: Although tens of malonyltransferases have been identified and functionally characterized in vitro (Luo et al., 2007; Manjasetty et al., 2012; Bontpart et al., 2015), their in vivo functions are largely unknown.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations indicating that while in vitro characterization exists, in vivo functions remain unclear.

claim: DTGs consist of a 17-hydroxygeranyllinalool aglycone that is decorated at the C3 and C17 hydroxyl positions by glucose, which in turn is modified by glucose, rhamnose and malonyl moieties, in various combinations.
source: DTGs consist of a 17-hydroxygeranyllinalool aglycone that is decorated at the C3 and C17 hydroxyl positions by glucose, which in turn is modified by glucose, rhamnose and malonyl moieties, in various combinations (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This structural description is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 46 different DTGs (21 chemical formulas and several structural isomers) have been characterized in Nicotiana attenuata.
source: So far, 46 different DTGs (21 chemical formulas and several structural isomers) have been characterized in Nicotiana attenuata, an ecological model plant with a rich portfolio of specialized metabolites
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and references previous characterization work.

claim: Lyciumoside IV and its malonylated products, Nicotianoside I and Nicotianoside II, constitute more than 80% of the DTG pool in N. attenuata.
source: however, the glycoside Lyciumoside IV and its malonylated products, Nicotianoside I and Nicotianoside II, constitute more than 80% of the DTG pool (Poreddy et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Poreddy et al., 2015.

claim: DTGs function in resistance against the specialist herbivore, tobacco hornworm (Manduca sexta) in N. attenuata.
source: In N. attenuata, DTGs function in resistance against the specialist herbivore, tobacco hornworm (Manduca sexta) (Lou and Baldwin, 2003; Jassbi et al., 2008; Heiling et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to Lou and Baldwin, 2003; Jassbi et al., 2008; Heiling et al., 2010.

claim: Malonylated DTGs are particularly strongly induced by M. sexta feeding and jasmonate signaling.
source: The malonylated DTGs are particularly strongly induced by M. sexta feeding and jasmonate signaling (Heiling et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Heiling et al., 2010.

claim: The malonyl moieties of DTGs are lost from the DTGs soon after their ingestion by M. sexta larvae due to the alkaline environment of M. sexta oral secretions and midgut.
source: The malonyl moieties of DTGs are lost from the DTGs soon after their ingestion by M. sexta larvae due to the alkaline environment of M. sexta oral secretions and midgut (Poreddy et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Poreddy et al., 2015.

claim: The loss of malonyl moieties from DTGs after ingestion by M. sexta rules out a central role for malonylation of DTGs in antiherbivore defense.
source: This observation rules out a central role for malonylation of DTGs in antiherbivore defense, and suggests that other arenas need to be explored for potential functions mediated by this malonylation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that malonyl groups are lost after ingestion.

claim: The insect feeding-induced glucosinolate breakdown product, indole-3-carbinol, arrests growth by interacting with the auxin receptor Transport Inhibitor Response (TIR1) as an auxin antagonist.
source: For example, the insect feeding-induced glucosinolate breakdown product, indole-3-carbinol, arrests growth by interacting with the auxin receptor Transport Inhibitor Response (TIR1) as an auxin antagonist (Katz et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Katz et al., 2015.

claim: Arabidopsis glucosinolates are thought to modulate plant biomass, flowering time and the circadian clock, and inhibit root growth.
source: Arabidopsis glucosinolates are also thought to modulate plant biomass, flowering time and the circadian clock, and inhibit root growth (Kerwin et al., 2011; Jensen et al., 2015; Francisco et al., 2016; Malinovsky et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to Kerwin et al., 2011; Jensen et al., 2015; Francisco et al., 2016; Malinovsky et al., 2017.

claim: Hyper-accumulation of flavonoids is associated with stunted growth and developmental abnormalities, which are assumed to result from effects on auxin transport.
source: Hyper-accumulation of flavonoids is associated with stunted growth and developmental abnormalities, which are assumed to result from effects on auxin transport (Franke et al., 2002; Bonawitz et al., 2014; Steenackers et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Franke et al., 2002; Bonawitz et al., 2014; Steenackers et al., 2017.

claim: Jasmonate signaling-deficient genotypes of N. attenuata have short styles, resulting in reduced fertility.
source: Jasmonate signaling-deficient genotypes of N. attenuata, including RNAi lines targeting ALLENE OXIDE CYCLASE (irAOC) and CORONATINE INSENSITIVE 1 (irCOI1), and ectopic expression of Arabidopsis JASMONIC ACID METHYL TRANSFERASE (JMT) and simultaneous silencing of METHYL JASMONATE ESTERASE (MJE) (JMT/mje) which dramatically decreased JA signaling, are reported to have short styles, resulting in reduced fertility (Stitz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Stitz et al., 2014.

claim: Transgenic N. tabacum plants deficient in COI1 display short styles.
source: Transgenic N. tabacum plants deficient in COI1 also display short styles (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2014.

claim: The mechanism of the Nicotiana genus-specific jasmonate-regulated short-style phenotype is completely obscure.
source: However, the mechanism of this seemingly Nicotiana genus-specific jasmonate-regulated phenotype is completely obscure.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Auxin plays a pivotal role throughout the entire lifespan of a plant, particularly in determination of floral development.
source: Auxin plays a pivotal role throughout the entire lifespan of a plant, particularly in determination of floral development.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about auxin function.

claim: Auxin can influence cell division, cell expansion and cell differentiation, and thereby regulate a wide spectrum of developmental processes.
source: It can influence cell division, cell expansion and cell differentiation, and thereby regulate a wide spectrum of developmental processes (Benjamins and Scheres, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Benjamins and Scheres, 2008.

claim: Mutants of AtPIN1 developed naked, pin-shaped inflorescences and abnormalities in all flower parts.
source: Mutants of AtPIN1, a polar auxin transporter, developed naked, pin-shaped inflorescences and abnormalities in all flower parts, confirming that auxin signaling contributes to flower development (Okada, 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Okada, 1991.

claim: Mutants of the auxin biosynthesis genes TRYPTOPHAN AMINOTRANSFERASE OF ARABIDOPSIS (TAA) and YUCCA display severe defects in floral patterning, and complete sterility.
source: Consistent with this, mutants of the auxin biosynthesis genes TRYPTOPHAN AMINOTRANSFERASE OF ARABIDOPSIS (TAA) and YUCCA display severe defects in floral patterning, and complete sterility (Cheng et al., 2006; Stepanova et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cheng et al., 2006; Stepanova et al., 2008.

claim: Auxin can regulate gynoecium morphogenesis, including style elongation, through a concentration gradient from the apical to the basal part of the gynoecium.
source: Auxin can also regulate gynoecium morphogenesis, including style elongation, through a concentration gradient from the apical to the basal part of the gynoecium (Nemhauser et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nemhauser et al., 2000.

claim: Although all types of malonylated DTGs increased after M. sexta elicitation, there was no difference in malonylation percentage between treatment and control.
source: Remarkably, although all types of malonylated DTGs increased after M. sexta elicitation, there was no difference in malonylation percentage between treatment and control.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1B and 1E.

claim: Total DTGs decreased dramatically over flower development, whereas the malonylation percentage was very stable.
source: Total DTGs decreased dramatically over flower development, whereas the malonylation percentage was very stable (Figure 1C and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and supported by data shown in Figure 1C and F.

claim: Different malonylated DTGs are highly variable across different tissues, with coefficients of variation (CV) ranging from 64 to 107.
source: By mining previously published metabolite data sets from different plant tissues (Li et al., 2016), we found that although different malonylated DTGs are highly variable across different tissues, with coefficients of variation (CV) ranging from 64 to 107 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–F)
evidence: This is stated in the Results and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–F.

claim: The malonylation percentage of DTGs was more uniform across tissues, with a CV of only 11, which is a significant outlier.
source: the malonylation percentage was more uniform, with a CV of only 11: a significant outlier (Figure 1—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2G.

claim: NIATv7_g22417 and NIATv7_g34586 shared the highest protein sequence identity with NtMaT1: 91.2% and 91.4%, respectively.
source: Among these MaTs, NIATv7_g22417 and NIATv7_g34586 shared the highest protein sequence identity with NtMaT1: 91.2% and 91.4%, respectively
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on sequence analysis.

claim: NIATv7_g13429 shared 80.6% protein sequence identity with NtMaT1.
source: followed by NIATv7_g13429, which shared 80.6% protein sequence identity with NtMaT1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Four of the candidate MaTs contained the two conserved BAHD enzyme motifs HXXXDG and DFGWG.
source: Protein sequence alignment showed that four of the candidate MaTs contained the two conserved BAHD enzyme motifs HXXXDG and DFGWG, but not NIATv7_g21823, which had only a HXXXDG motif near the protein's center portion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: NIATv7_g39356 and NIATv7_g21823 contained the flavonoid acyltransferase conserved motif, YFGNC.
source: Notably, two putative MaTs, NIATv7_ g39356 and g21823, which share the highest identity with NtMaT1, also contained the flavonoid acyltransferase conserved motif, YFGNC (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: NaMaT1, NaMaT2 and NaMaT3 could catalyze malonylation from Lyciumoside IV to its monomalonylated form, Nicotianoside I, together with a comparatively minor production of the dimalonylated form, Nicotianoside II.
source: Consistent with the expression patterns, the in vitro recombinant enzyme activity show that the same three genes: NaMaT1, NaMaT2 and NaMaT3 could catalyze malonylation from Lyciumoside IV to its monomalonylated form, Nicotianoside I, together with a comparatively minor production of the dimalonylated form, Nicotianoside II (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and demonstrated by in vitro enzyme assays shown in Figure 2C.

claim: NaMaT1 was strongly induced within 5 hr after the onset of M. sexta larval feeding (59-fold), and then slightly decreased by 9 hr.
source: NaMaT1 was strongly induced within 5 hr after the onset of M. sexta larval feeding (59-fold), and then slightly decreased by 9 hr (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2D using RNA-seq data.

claim: Both NaMaT2 and NaMaT3 transcripts were suppressed by M. sexta feeding.
source: In contrast, both NaMaT2 and NaMaT3 transcripts were suppressed by M. sexta feeding, which is opposite to the dynamics of the M. sexta-induced DTG profile (Figure 2D and Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The transcript abundance of NaMaT1 in VIGS-NaMaT1 plants decreased more than 80% compared with VIGS controls.
source: The transcript abundance of NaMaT1 in VIGS-NaMaT1 plants (VIGS-MaT1) decreased more than 80% compared with VIGS controls (empty vector, VIGS-EV), without affecting the abundance of NaMaT2 or NaMaT3 transcripts (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: NaGLS transcript abundance significantly increased in VIGS-MaT1 leaves.
source: Notably, we also analyzed transcript abundance of two other reported DTG biosynthesis genes, geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase (NaGGPPS) (Jassbi et al., 2008) and geranyllinalool synthase (NaGLS) (Falara et al., 2014) in VIGS plants, and found that NaGLS transcript abundance significantly increased in VIGS-MaT1 leaves (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: VIGS-MaT1 plants rarely produced capsules.
source: However, we observed that VIGS-MaT1 plants rarely produced capsules.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and quantified in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Styles of VIGS-MaT1 plants were extremely short, less than half the length of VIGS-EV styles.
source: In a second experiment, we determined that styles of VIGS-MaT1 plants were extremely short, less than half the length of VIGS-EV styles (Figure 3A and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3A and E.

claim: The stylar cell length was strongly reduced in VIGS-MaT1 plants, whereas cell number was not.
source: The stylar cell length was strongly reduced, whereas cell number was not (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3B–D using microscopy.

claim: The short-style phenotype vanished in irGGPPS-background VIGS-MaT1 plants.
source: The results show that the short-style phenotype vanished in irGGPPS-background VIGS-MaT1 plants (Figure 3)
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Silencing NaMaT1 significantly reduced the malonylation percentage, primarily through an increase in DTGs with low malonylation degree (core and monomalonylated DTGs).
source: Silencing NaMaT1 significantly reduced the malonylation percentage, primarily through an increase in DTGs with low malonylation degree (core and monomalonylated DTGs), in comparison to VIGS-EV controls (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The effect of NaMaT1 silencing on malonylation percentage was more pronounced after leaves were treated with MeJA.
source: This effect was more pronounced after leaves were treated with MeJA (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Core and monomalonylated DTGs increased in inflorescences and styles with stigmas of VIGS-MaT1 plants.
source: In addition to increasing core and monomalonylated DTGs, dimalonylated and trimalonylated DTGs significantly decreased in inflorescences and styles with stigmas, leading to a dramatic decrease in malonylation percentage in VIGS-MaT1 in comparison to VIGS-EV (Figure 4C,D)
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Dimalonylated and trimalonylated DTGs significantly decreased in inflorescences and styles with stigmas of VIGS-MaT1 plants.
source: In addition to increasing core and monomalonylated DTGs, dimalonylated and trimalonylated DTGs significantly decreased in inflorescences and styles with stigmas, leading to a dramatic decrease in malonylation percentage in VIGS-MaT1 in comparison to VIGS-EV (Figure 4C,D)
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: All individual core and monomalonyated DTGs were dramatically increased in VIGS-MaT1 styles, whereas trimalonylated DTGs were no longer detectable.
source: all individual core and monomalonyated DTGs were dramatically increased in VIGS-MaT1 styles, whereas trimalonylated DTGs were no longer detectable (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: VIGS of NaMaT1 reduced JA and JA-Ile levels significantly in inflorescences compared with the VIGS-EV, without affecting IAA contents.
source: VIGS of NaMaT1 reduced JA and JA-Ile levels significantly in inflorescences compared with the VIGS-EV, without affecting IAA contents (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: VIGS of NaMaT1 reduced IAA levels in styles and stigmas by 40%, but had no significant effect on JAs levels.
source: In contrast, VIGS of NaMaT1 reduced IAA levels in styles and stigmas by 40%, but had no significant effect on JAs levels (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Styles and stigmas contained the highest levels of IAA among all the measured tissues, about 6.5-fold more than that of the S1 leaf.
source: Styles and stigmas contained the highest levels of IAA among all the measured tissues, about 6.5-fold more than that of the S1 leaf (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: While IAA decreased in VIGS-MaT1 of EV plants, Trp levels increased dramatically.
source: While IAA decreased in VIGS-MaT1 of EV plants, Trp levels increased dramatically (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The differences in IAA and Trp levels were eliminated when NaMaT1 was silenced in the irGGPPS background.
source: These differences were eliminated when we silenced NaMaT1 in the irGGPPS background (Figure 5A and B)
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: NaTAA1 activity was similar between EV and VIGS-MaT1.
source: Surprisingly, NaTAA1 activity was similar between EV and VIGS-MaT1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results based on in vitro enzyme assays.

claim: The transformation from IPA to IAA, which is thought to be catalyzed by YUCCA, was significantly impaired in VIGS-MaT1 style.
source: However, the transformation from IPA to IAA, which is thought to be catalyzed by YUCCA, was significantly impaired in VIGS-MaT1 style (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 5C using in vitro enzyme assays.

claim: Exogenous application IAA approximately restored the short styles to their normal lengths.
source: Exogenous application IAA approximately restored the short styles to their normal lengths (Figure 5D)
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Exogenous IAA application did not affect the malonylation degree of stylar DTGs.
source: without affecting the malonylation degree of stylar DTGs (Figure 5E)
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In both herbivore-damaged and control leaves, malonylation percentages in irAOC were significantly higher than in EV plants.
source: In both herbivore-damaged and control leaves, malonylation percentages in irAOC were significantly higher than in EV plants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In flower buds, the irAOC malonylation percentage was significantly higher than in EV.
source: In flower buds, the irAOC malonylation percentage was also significantly higher than in EV (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: MeJA treatment could partially restore the irAOC short style phenotype.
source: MeJA treatment could partially restore the irAOC short style phenotype (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and [Stitz et al., 2014])
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, with support from Stitz et al., 2014.

claim: MeJA treatment partially restored the malonylation percentages towards EV levels in irAOC plants.
source: and also partially restored the malonylation percentages towards EV levels (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The malonylation percentage of irAOC styles was significantly higher than in EV.
source: In line with leaves and flower buds, the malonylation percentage of irAOC styles was also significantly higher than in EV (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Silencing NaMaT1 in EV or irAOC plants resulted in similarly truncated styles.
source: To further test this hypothesis, we compared style lengths in VIGS-MaT1 and VIGS-EV of both EV and irAOC plants. Silencing NaMaT1 in EV or irAOC plants resulted in similarly truncated styles (Figure 6B and Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6B and Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The malonylation percentages after VIGS-MaT1 in both EV and irAOC backgrounds were similar, much lower than the VIGS-EV of both EV and irAOC genetic backgrounds.
source: Consistently, the malonylation percentages after VIGS-MaT1 in both EV and irAOC backgrounds were similar, much lower than the VIGS-EV of both EV and irAOC genetic backgrounds (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: MeJA treatment could partially restore irAOC-EV short styles, but not the short styles of VIGS-MaT1 in irAOC or EV plants.
source: Furthermore, MeJA treatment could partially restore irAOC-EV short styles, but not the short styles of VIGS-MaT1 in irAOC or EV plants (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: NaMaT1 functions downstream of NaAOC to control style length.
source: These data revealed that NaMaT1 functions downstream of NaAOC to control style length.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that MeJA cannot rescue VIGS-MaT1 short styles.

claim: When irAOC was crossed with irGGPPS to silence both DTG and JA production, the irAOC short-style phenotype was completely restored to normal style lengths of EV or WT plants.
source: Importantly, when we crossed irAOC with irGGPPS to silence both DTG and JA production, the irAOC short-style phenotype was completely restored to normal style lengths of EV or WT plants (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: IAA levels in irAOC styles were much lower than in EV.
source: Because the VIGS-MaT1 short style phenotype results from attenuated IAA levels, we measured IAA contents in irAOC styles. IAA levels in irAOC styles were much lower than in EV (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The protein activity responsible for transforming IPA to IAA was marginally decreased in irAOC styles compared to that in EV.
source: The protein activity responsible for transforming IPA to IAA was marginally decreased in irAOC styles compared to that in EV (Figure 6G)
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6G using in vitro enzyme assays.

claim: Exogenous applications of IAA partially restored the truncated styles of irAOC plants to WT lengths.
source: Finally, exogenous applications of IAA partially restored the truncated styles of irAOC plants to WT lengths (Figure 6H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Enzyme assays showed that three MaT proteins, NaMaT1-3, catalyze the first step of DTG malonylation, from Lyciumoside IV to Nicotianoside I, and the second step, from Nicotianoside I to Nicotianoside II, in vitro.
source: Enzyme assays showed that three MaT proteins, NaMaT1-3, catalyze the first step of DTG malonylation, from Lyciumoside IV to Nicotianoside I, and the second step, from Nicotianoside I to Nicotianoside II, in vitro (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: In vivo silencing of NaMaT1 dramatically decreased dimalonylated and trimalonylated DTGs in inflorescences and styles, which indicates that NaMaT1 might also control the third step of the malonylation reaction in planta.
source: However, in vivo silencing of NaMaT1 dramatically decreased dimalonylated and trimalonylated DTGs in inflorescences and styles (Figure 4), which indicates that NaMaT1 might also control the third step of the malonylation reaction in planta.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from the in vivo data in Figure 4.

claim: NaMaT1 is a malonyl-CoA:DTG malonyltransferase, which may catalyze three consecutive malonylation steps.
source: Based on our current results, we infer that NaMaT1 is a malonyl-CoA:DTG malonyltransferase, which may catalyze three consecutive malonylation steps, as reported for Dm3MaT2, which catalyzes consecutive dimalonyl transfers to anthocyanin (Suzuki et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from the results, with comparison to Dm3MaT2.

claim: NbMaT1 and NtMaT1 share the highest sequence similarity with NaMaT2 and NaMaT3, about 90%, whereas the identity with NaMaT1 is 80%.
source: Phylogenic and protein identity analysis showed that NbMaT1 and NtMaT1 share the highest sequence similarity with NaMaT2 and NaMaT3, about 90%, whereas the identity with NaMaT1 is 80% (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Cross-tissue comprehensive nontargeted metabolomics analyses did not reveal any malonylated flavonoids in N. attenuata.
source: Moreover, cross-tissue comprehensive nontargeted metabolomics analyses did not reveal any malonylated flavonoids in N. attenuata (Li et al., 2016)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation to Li et al., 2016.

claim: NaMaT1 mainly functions in DTG malonylation in planta.
source: Thus, we assume that NaMaT1 mainly functions in DTG malonylation in planta
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from the lack of malonylated flavonoids and expression patterns.

claim: NaMaT2 and NaMaT3 could also accept aromatic glycosides as substrates, like NbMaT1 and NtMaT1.
source: and NaMaT2 and NaMaT3 could also accept aromatic glycosides as substrates, like NbMaT1 and NtMaT1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as speculation based on sequence similarity.

claim: Silencing a rhamnosyltransferase gene inhibits the transcript accumulation of all upstream genes in DTG biosynthesis.
source: For the regulation of DTG biosynthesis, feed-back and feed-forward regulation are both described by Heiling et al. (in preparation): silencing a rhamnosyltransferase gene inhibits the transcript accumulation of all upstream genes
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and attributed to Heiling et al. (in preparation).

claim: Silencing NaGGPPS suppresses transcript accumulation of downstream biosynthetic genes in DTG biosynthesis.
source: and silencing NaGGPPS also suppresses transcript accumulation of downstream biosynthetic genes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and attributed to Heiling et al. (in preparation).

claim: VIGS of NaMaT1 tended to increase both NaMaT2 and NaMaT3 expression.
source: Here, we show that VIGS of NaMaT1 tended to increase both NaMaT2 and NaMaT3 expression, and significantly increased NaGLS expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: The induction of NaMaT1 and suppression of NaMaT2 and NaMaT3 in response to M. sexta feeding may represent a homeostatic mechanism to control DTG malonylation percentage during the response to herbivore attack.
source: Here, the induction of NaMaT1 and suppression of NaMaT2 and NaMaT3 in response to M. sexta feeding may represent a similar mechanism to control DTG malonylation percentage during the response to herbivore attack (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from the expression patterns in Figure 2D.

claim: A malonylation percentage alteration as low as 4.1% in irAOC is associated with a drastically shortened style and infertility.
source: This is likely important because a malonylation percentage alteration as low as 4.1% in irAOC is associated with a drastically shortened style and infertility (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 6A.

claim: Both high (irAOC) and low (VIGS-MaT1) malonylation percentages were accompanied by truncated styles.
source: Importantly, both high (irAOC) and low (VIGS-MaT1) malonylation percentages were accompanied by truncated styles.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The total abundance of DTGs in irGGPPS inflorescences may not be enough to affect style development, regardless of their malonylation.
source: We think that this is because irGGPPS plants produce much lower levels of DTGs, and thus the total abundance of DTGs in inflorescences may not be enough to affect style development, regardless of their malonylation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an explanation for why irGGPPS-MaT1 does not show short styles.

claim: Induction of the jasmonate signaling pathway strongly induced NaMaT1 expression and DTG malonylation.
source: Induction of the jasmonate signaling pathway, including via MeJA treatment and M. sexta attack, strongly induced NaMaT1 expression (Figure 2D) and DTG malonylation (Figure 1B), indicating that NaMaT1 is responsible for the increase in malonylated DTGs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 2D and Figure 1B.

claim: High-dose MeJA treatment suppressed malonylation percentages.
source: However, as noted above, high-dose MeJA treatment suppressed malonylation percentages
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and refers to data in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Silencing JA biosynthesis (irAOC) increased malonylation percentage in many tissues.
source: and silencing JA biosynthesis (irAOC) increased malonylation percentage in many tissues (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Other MaTs also contribute to the DTG malonylation process.
source: This apparent contradiction may be explained by the possibility that other MaTs also contribute to the DTG malonylation process
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference to explain the complex regulation of malonylation.

claim: Although NaMaT1 transcript accumulation decreased more than 80% in VIGS-MaT1 leaves, the malonylation percentage was only reduced by 19.6%.
source: Although NaMaT1 transcript accumulation decreased more than 80% in VIGS-MaT1 leaves (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), the malonylation percentage was only reduced by 19.6% (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and Figure 4B.

claim: The truncated style phenotype results from the low auxin levels found in the styles, which in turn are due to reduced IAA biosynthesis.
source: Our experiments shed light on this phenomenon by demonstrating that the DTG biosynthesis specific NaGGPPS is required for the development of the truncated style phenotype (Figure 3), and this truncated style phenotype results from the low auxin levels found in the styles, which in turn are due to reduced IAA biosynthesis (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 3 and Figure 5.

claim: The style-specific effect of NaMaT1 silencing occurs because the style synthesizes large amounts of DTGs.
source: We hypothesize that this style-specific effect occurs because the style synthesizes large amounts of DTGs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a hypothesis and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: VIGS-MaT1 results in a stronger decrease in malonylation percentage in styles than it does in leaves.
source: and VIGS-MaT1 results in a stronger decrease in malonylation percentage in styles than it does in leaves (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by comparison of data in Figure 4B and 4D.

claim: Styles are likely the auxin source for at least the gynoecium, as predicted by the apical-basal gradient of auxin theory.
source: In addition, styles contained the highest levels of IAA of all tissues analyzed (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) and are likely the auxin source for at least the gynoecium, as predicted by the apical-basal gradient of auxin theory (Nemhauser et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 and citation to Nemhauser et al., 2000.

claim: Data from irGGPPS plants with depleted DTGs supports the hypothesis that the truncated style of VIGS-MaT1 is related to DTGs.
source: Our data from irGGPPS plants with depleted DTGs supports our hypothesis that the truncated style of VIGS-MaT1 is related to DTGs
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and refers to data in Figure 3.

claim: The exact molecular events that lead to the short-style phenotype remain unknown.
source: but the exact molecular events that lead to this phenomenon remain unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a knowledge gap.

claim: The biosynthesis and malonylation of DTGs may interact with other compounds from the diterpenoid pathway, especially some phytohormones, like strigolactones, abscisic acid, cytokinins, gibberellins and brassinosteroids.
source: The biosynthesis and malonylation of DTGs, which are diterpenoid derivatives, may interact with other compounds from this pathway, especially some phytohormones, like strigolactones, abscisic acid, cytokinins, gibberellins and brassinosteroids (Cazzonelli and Pogson, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as speculation with a citation to Cazzonelli and Pogson, 2010.

claim: Flavonoids are the only known secondary metabolites that could inhibit auxin transport, resulting in stunted growth in Arabidopsis, Medicago, tomato and apple.
source: Notably, flavonoids were thus far the only known secondary metabolites that could inhibit auxin transport, resulting in stunted growth in Arabidopsis, Medicago, tomato and apple (Brown et al., 2001; Eckardt, 2006; Besseau et al., 2007; Schijlen et al., 2007; Dare et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Flavonoids did not significantly increase in VIGS-MaT1 plants.
source: However, flavonoids did not significantly increase in VIGS-MaT1 plants (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Rutin has been reported not to affect auxin transport.
source: and levels of rutin even decreased. Rutin has been reported not to affect auxin transport (Jacobs and Rubery, 1988).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation to Jacobs and Rubery, 1988.

claim: The short style phenotype is a malonylation-dependent phenotype that is based specifically on DTGs.
source: In summary, the short style phenotype is a malonylation-dependent phenotype that is based specifically on DTGs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: By shortening styles by titrating the degree of malonyl DTG decorations, plants may be able to regulate their outcrossing rates in response to environmental factors that influence JA signaling or DTGs accumulation, such as herbivory rates.
source: At a functional level, by shortening styles by titrating the degree of malonyl DTG decorations, plants may be able to regulate their outcrossing rates in response to environmental factors that influence JA signaling or DTGs accumulation, such as herbivory rates.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as speculation about the ecological function.

claim: Abnormal JA signaling could dysregulate DTG malonylation patterns, thereby affecting plant style development via auxin signaling.
source: Our work demonstrates that abnormal JA signaling could dysregulate DTG malonylation patterns, thereby affecting plant style development via auxin signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a summary of the findings.

claim: Decorations of plant specialized metabolites can be tuned to remarkably uniform levels.
source: Decorations of plant specialized metabolites can be tuned to remarkably uniform levels, and this regulation plays a central but poorly understood role in controlling the development of specific plant parts, such as floral styles.
evidence: This is stated in the Abstract as a main conclusion of the study.

claim: The regulation of specialized metabolite decorations plays a central but poorly understood role in controlling the development of specific plant parts, such as floral styles.
source: Decorations of plant specialized metabolites can be tuned to remarkably uniform levels, and this regulation plays a central but poorly understood role in controlling the development of specific plant parts, such as floral styles.
evidence: This is stated in the Abstract as a main conclusion of the study.

claim: The malonyl residue is thought to confer structural diversity, stability, and solubility to the decorated metabolites and provide a means of detoxifying xenobiotics.
source: The malonyl residue is thought to confer structural diversity, stability, and solubility to the decorated metabolites and provide a means of detoxifying xenobiotics (Suzuki et al., 2002; Taguchi et al., 2005; Koirala et al., 2014; Suzuki et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: In plant specialized metabolism, the malonyl group is largely transferred from malonyl-coenzyme A (Malonyl-CoA) to the C'6 of the glycosyl moiety of glucoconjugates.
source: In plant specialized metabolism, the malonyl group is largely transferred from malonyl-coenzyme A (Malonyl-CoA) to the C'6 of the glycosyl moiety of glucoconjugates (Taguchi et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by a citation to Taguchi et al., 2005.

claim: 17-hydroxygeranyllinalool diterpene glycosides (DTGs) are abundant (mg/g FW) secondary metabolites in green tissues of many solanaceous plants, including tobacco (Nicotiana spp.), pepper (Capsicum annuum) and wolfberry (Lycium chinense).
source: 17-hydroxygeranyllinalool diterpene glycosides (DTGs) are abundant (mg/g FW) secondary metabolites in green tissues of many solanaceous plants, including tobacco (Nicotiana spp.), pepper (Capsicum annuum) and wolfberry (Lycium chinense) (Jassbi et al., 2006; Lee et al., 2008; Heiling et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to Jassbi et al., 2006; Lee et al., 2008; Heiling et al., 2010.

claim: Only the Nicotiana genus produces DTGs among species for which JA-deficient phenotypes have been reported.
source: Among species for which JA-deficient phenotypes have been reported, only the genus Nicotiana produces DTGs (Heiling et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and supported by a citation to Heiling et al., 2016.

claim: Pollen from either VIGS-MaT1 or VIGS-EV plants applied to the VIGS-EV pistil produced normal capsules and similar numbers of seeds in each capsule.
source: Pollen from either VIGS-MaT1 or VIGS-EV plants applied to the VIGS-EV pistil produced normal capsules and similar numbers of seeds in each capsule (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: Only withered capsules resulted from hand-pollination of VIGS-MaT1 pistils with VIGS-EV pollen.
source: However, only withered capsules resulted from hand-pollination of VIGS-MaT1 pistils with VIGS-EV pollen
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: No capsules resulted from pollination of VIGS-MaT1 pistils with VIGS-MaT1 pollen.
source: and no capsules resulted from pollination of VIGS-MaT1 pistils with VIGS-MaT1 pollen.
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The withered capsules from VIGS-MaT1 pistils produced dramatically fewer seeds than those of VIGS-EV capsules.
source: The withered capsules produced dramatically fewer seeds than those of VIGS-EV capsules, although the seed germination rate was not significantly affected (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: The seed germination rate was not significantly affected in VIGS-MaT1 plants.
source: although the seed germination rate was not significantly affected (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The transcript abundance of YUC-like 2 was similar between VIGS-MaT1 and VIGS-EV in both backgrounds of irGGPPS and EV plants.
source: The transcript abundance of YUC-like 2 was similar between VIGS-MaT1 and VIGS-EV in both backgrounds of irGGPPS and EV plants (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Brassinolide treatment did not recover the short style phenotype of VIGS-MaT1.
source: To test whether brassinosteroids may contribute to the VIGS-MaT1 style phenotype in other ways, we exogenously applied brassinolide to VIGS-MaT1 flower buds. This treatment did not recover the short style phenotype of VIGS-MaT1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2D.
